structured_output.summary: Phase 10 (Red Team vendor contracts and model evolution) meets its stated acceptance criteria with independently verifiable evidence. The pinned 0.93.0 source bytes/hash/size match the Phase 9 pin exactly and are re-verified at generation time along with the MIT notice hash and a canonical-JSON↔YAML equality check using a triple-asserted js-yaml 4.3.2 pin (package.json, lockfile, installed package). The 47-operation recount is produced twice by independent implementations (Python generator and a standalone Node script), and the eleven added route identities are matched against the accepted plan's markdown table rather than a hand-written count. The operation ledger has exactly 47 rows with per-operation parameters, request/response schemas, native class/method, source hash and an implemented flag; the 11 `implemented: false` rows are precisely the Phase 11 routes. The OpenAPI lowering compiler is small, deterministic and fails closed on unsupported keywords, remote refs, recursion, non-string enums, undiscriminated oneOf and pointer reuse, each with an adversarial test. Frozen graph nodes and roots are provably unchanged while vendor roots live in a separate `vendor:red-team-dp:0.93.0:` namespace. Exactly four response-presence waivers exist, are enforced in generation, fail closed on a fifth, and are tested in Rust to apply only to response modes and only to those four fields (JobResponseSchema `uuid` omission still rejected under the compatible root). Model evidence is genuinely independent: 1636 AJV-2020 specimens derived from the pinned spec (1054 negative), cross-validated by the Node checker and by the native validator, with typed decode, JSON round-trip and redacted-Debug assertions across 152 roots. Additive evolution of legacy models is generated and ledgered (model-additions.json), including the planned optional typed `categories` on `RemediationDetail` with the public return type preserved. All twelve legacy query parameters that now fail before credentials have a negative Rust test asserting `ErrorKind::Validation`, `RemoteOutcome::NotSent`, zero transport calls and zero token provider calls; rejection is structural (spec-generated closed query objects), not hand-coded. The 25-command gate matches `tools/check_phase.py` exactly, all commands exited 0, and I confirmed the recorded Rust test counts against the raw check report rather than the prose. Remaining weaknesses are secondary hardening and bookkeeping items, not unmet criteria: negative vendor specimens are only asserted to be rejected under Mode::Request, the rejected-parameter ledger is hand-maintained with a circular test (I manually confirmed the current twelve are complete), the newly-required-field fail-closed inspects only component-level `required` (no nested `required` arrays exist in this pin, so no present impact), and the `implemented` probe is a file-scoped regex. CHANGELOG entries and the 0.2.0 version bump are explicitly Phase 12 scope and were not judged here.

findings.description: The generated vendor model probe stops at `if !valid{continue;}`, so all ~1054 negative specimens are only asserted to be rejected under Mode::Request. Response validation is the policy actually applied to wire payloads in `engine::decode_contract`, and it is deliberately looser (open enums plus the four presence waivers). Outside the five hand-written assertions in `red_team_contracts.rs:1631-1695`, no negative specimen exercises Mode::Response or Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults, so a future relaxation leaking into the response graph (for example a closed object silently becoming passthrough, or a required field becoming optional) would not be caught by the 1636-case corpus.
findings.required_fix: Extend the generated probe so that negative specimens are also asserted under Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults for the categories where the response policy is defined to be identical. Label each case in make-red-team-fixtures.mjs with its mutation class (missing_required, wrong_type, closed_object, bound_violation, format_violation) and, in the probe, require response-mode rejection for closed_object, bound_violation and format_violation cases, and for missing_required cases other than the four reviewed waiver pairs. Regenerate via `python tools/red_team_dataplane.py` (no manual edits to the generated Rust).

findings.description: The per-parameter disposition ledger is driven by the hand-written REJECTED dict, and `tools/test_red_team_dataplane.py:82` asserts the generated `rejectedLegacyParameters` equals REJECTED — the ledger is compared against its own input. Nothing derives the set of native option fields that no longer map to a declared query parameter in the pinned spec. The plan requires enumerating every existing parameter absent from the current spec and giving it an explicit disposition. I manually compared every red-team option struct (AttackListOptions, GoalListOptions, RedTeamListOptions, RedTeamScanListOptions, PromptSetsReportOptions, PromptsBySetListOptions, CustomAttacksReportListOptions, ScanStatisticsOptions, ScoreTrendOptions) against `crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/contract.json` and confirmed the current twelve are complete, so runtime behavior is correct today; the risk is that a future pin silently drops an option from the ledger and from the CHANGELOG disposition requirement while still rejecting it at runtime.
findings.required_fix: Derive the rejected set instead of declaring it: parse the public option-struct field names per native method (or declare the method→option-field map once) and compute `fields - contract.queryKinds` as the rejected list, then keep REJECTED only as a reviewed expectation that generation must match. Make `test_all_unsupported_parameters_are_closed_pre_auth_errors` fail when a derived rejected parameter is absent from REJECTED.

findings.description: `changed_contracts` computes newly-required fields only from each component schema's top-level `required` array (`value.get("required", [])`). Nested inline object schemas inside components are not scanned, and the WAIVERS lookup in `_compile` likewise only matches component-root pointers (`component = pointer.removeprefix("#/components/schemas/")`). I confirmed by grep that the pinned openapi.json contains no `required` array below component level, so there is no present impact; however the fifth-waiver fail-closed guard the plan relies on would not trigger for a nested newly-required field at the next pin, and such a field would tighten response decoding for older deployments without a recorded classification.
findings.required_fix: Walk the full schema closure (components plus inline operation request/response schemas) when collecting `required` sets for the before/after comparison, and key the waiver lookup on the schema pointer rather than only on component names, so any newly required field anywhere in the reachable closure stops generation.

findings.description: The `implemented` flag in the 47-row ledger is computed with `re.search(r"pub async fn " + member)` over the whole module file, without scoping to the impl block of the row's `nativeClass`. Today each red-team module hosts a single client, so the result is correct, but the probe would report an operation as implemented if an unrelated client in the same module happened to expose a same-named method. This flag is the gate for `--require-complete` in Phase 11.
findings.required_fix: Scope the search to the `impl <nativeClass> {` block (or resolve the method through the generated binding map) so that the implemented flag is bound to the exact class and method recorded in the ledger row.

findings.description: Every entry in schema-diff.json receives one of two constant disposition strings ('current_vendor_validation_and_typed_models' for schema changes, 'current_vendor_client_contract' for operation changes). The diff therefore enumerates all 166 changes but the recorded classification carries no per-change information, so the plan's 'fail on unclassified changes' requirement is satisfied only for the newly-required-field class and the unsupported-keyword class.
findings.required_fix: Derive a discriminated disposition per change (added_schema, removed_schema, added_optional_property, enum_values_added, bound_changed, type_changed, root_shape_changed, …) and fail generation on any change whose derived class is not in a reviewed allow-list, so that a genuinely novel change class stops the gate rather than inheriting a blanket label.

findings.description: The phase 10 record lists qualification_attempts 02 and 03 but omits attempt 01, whose check report is retained on disk as docs/checks/phase-10-attempt-01-before-g10.json, and there is no reference to the orphaned docs/reviews/phase-10-attempt-01.prompt.md (no corresponding .cli.json or review record exists). AGENTS.md requires recording the review artifact, checks and outcome for each attempt in docs/phase-status.json, and every other phase in the file lists its review_attempts.
findings.required_fix: Add the attempt-01 check report to the phase 10 qualification_attempts list with its status and resolution, and either record docs/reviews/phase-10-attempt-01.prompt.md under a review_attempts entry with its actual outcome (including that no CLI result was produced) or remove the orphaned prompt so the phase record accounts for every retained artifact.
